results.reader_title: EU research rapporteurs press Berlin to safeguard 2028–34 Horizon Europe
results.reader_what: Christian Ehler and René Repasi met German government representatives, including the Chancellor’s office, to lobby against disproportionate Horizon Europe cuts.
results.reader_why: The German budget stance could influence the eventual scale and institutional autonomy of the EU’s next seven-year research programme.
results.reader_more: In the week of 2 November 2026, rapporteurs from the two main Parliament political groups jointly approached German coalition interlocutors before 2028–34 Multiannual Financial Framework talks. They urged protection of EU research funding and separation of Horizon Europe from industrial-policy priorities in the planned European Competitiveness Fund. Competing Horizon Europe budget positions were €177bn (Parliament), €155bn (Commission) and €140bn (Irish Council presidency), each in 2025 prices; no final budget or German commitment resulted.
